title: Which patient?
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on a cardiology ward at night. The medical registrar, busy in the emergency department, phones and asks you to stop the heparin infusion for the patient in bed 4 "before his operation tomorrow", then hangs up.

Mr Hughes in bed 4 has an NSTEMI, isn't having an operation, and has had more chest pain this evening. The registrar can be phoned back.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 4 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Stop the infusion as asked, as the registrar is more senior.
options.detailed: Stopping anticoagulation in a patient with ongoing chest pain from an NSTEMI could be dangerous, and the instruction seems to be a mix-up. It is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Ask the nurse in charge what she thinks you should do.
options.brief: Delays clarifying with the person who gave the instruction.
options.detailed: The nurse may agree it seems wrong, but she can't change the registrar's plan. It ranks third.

options.text: Keep the infusion running and ask the consultant for advice.
options.brief: Safe, but goes around the registrar.
options.detailed: Not stopping the heparin protects Mr Hughes, but the registrar can be reached and is the right person to ask first. It ranks second.

options.text: Call the registrar back, describing Mr Hughes's symptoms.
options.brief: Likely a mix-up, which a quick call can resolve.
options.detailed: The instruction doesn't fit Mr Hughes, so it may be meant for another patient. Calling back with the key facts lets the registrar correct it. It ranks first.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you check an instruction that doesn't fit the patient, even when a busy senior gives it.
explanation.keyDetails: The instruction mentions an operation Mr Hughes isn't having. He has ongoing chest pain. The registrar can be reached.
explanation.reasoning: [D] checks with the person who gave the instruction, and [C] keeps him safe but bypasses the registrar. [B] delays, and [A] could harm him.
explanation.competing: Some would rank [C] first because it protects him straight away. The key puts [D] first because the registrar is available and the infusion hasn't been stopped yet.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 1, acting when you believe an instruction may be unsafe.
